subject: Operator minimum privileges & key redelivery playbook for VPC/on‑prem deploy
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@northfield.health>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Cheng <mcheng@northfield.health>, Legal <legal@northfield.health>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy: operator privileges + key handback questions

Jonas,

Thanks for walking us through the Private deployment options yesterday. Two follow-ups from our security and legal teams before we move to an SOW:

1) Operator privileges: we need a concrete definition of the minimum set of operator actions required for day‑to‑day health checks vs. emergency break‑glass. Can you provide an ACL/matrix and the proposed RBAC model so we can map it to our internal controls?

2) Customer keys: Northfield will require customer‑managed keys (KMS/HSM) and a documented handback plan at contract termination. We also need to understand the exact mechanism for key redelivery / escrow, timeline, and verification steps (remote attestation, if applicable).

3) Subprocessor notifications: what advance notice do you provide for new subprocessors in private deployments, and does Redwood allow us to pre‑approve or restrict specific categories?

Could you send a short playbook (operational steps + who does what) we can share with our infosec and procurement teams?

Appreciate it,
Sarah Lin
Head of Security Programs
Northfield Health

---
Sent from my mobile
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@northfield.health>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy: operator privileges + key handback questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. High level responses below; attaching a short operator‑privs matrix and a draft handback checklist for your team to review.

Operator privileges (summary):
- Day‑to‑day monitoring: read‑only telemetry, log aggregation access (redacted), ability to restart runtime processes only within customer‑controlled orchestrator; no access to private key material or customer KMS metadata.
- Break‑glass (emergency): temporary, auditable elevation via a time‑boxed support token. Elevation requires two internal approvers and a documented justification; all actions are logged and a post‑event review is performed with the customer.
- Operator accounts are scoped per‑cluster and bound to ephemeral credentials; operators cannot export model weights or token payloads.

Customer keys and handback:
- Customer holds primary KEK in their HSM or cloud KMS. Redwood stores only wrapped keys (we cannot unwrap without a customer action unless break‑glass is invoked under the above process).
- Handback playbook (attached): coordinated export of wrapped key material, verification via key fingerprinting, and optional remote attestation report if HSM is used. Default handback window: 10 business days post‑termination unless expedited by mutual agreement.
- Escrow: we propose a signed, time‑limited escrow option (customer‑triggered) for customers who require a vaulted copy; technical controls and signing keys are defined in the playbook.

Subprocessors and notifications:
- For Private deployments in a VPC/on‑prem we limit subprocessors to the minimal set (support tooling, image registry mirrors, on‑site ops partners). We provide a rolling 30‑day notice for changes; for any subprocessor with access to metadata or logs we offer an opt‑out path as a procurement term where feasible.

Next steps: I attached the matrix and checklist. Kimberly — can you confirm whether the 10‑day handback timeline and the escrow language are OK from a legal/ procurement standpoint, or suggest redlines? Marissa / Karthik — please flag any operational gaps (remote attestation feasibility, telemetry redaction specifics).

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Security & Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-operator-privs-matrix.xlsx; handback-procedure-checklist.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@northfield.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@northfield.health>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy: operator privileges + key handback questions

Sarah — added a couple of legal/procurement notes inline and attached a marked‑up DPA extract (see dpa-redlines-northfield.pdf). High‑level:
- Handback timeline: request to make the 10 business days the default but allow a 5 business day expedited path at customer expense. Also proposing a certificate of destruction for any cached artifacts stored by Redwood during the transition window.
- Escrow: we will accept a customer‑triggered escrow but need to limit escrow access to a signed transfer event; escrow storage will require mutual S3/GCS encryption at rest and dual control for retrieval.
- Subprocessors: we can add a procurement term that requires Redwood notify Northfield and allow a 10‑day review/ objection window for subprocessors that have potential access to telemetry metadata.

Operational ask: Jonas / Marissa, can you add one paragraph on how telemetry is redacted (PII & payload tokens) before it's visible to on‑call or support staff? That will unblock Northfield's infosec.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dpa-redlines-northfield.pdf
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@northfield.health>

Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy: operator privileges + key handback questions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before we route to procurement:

1) HSM / remote attestation: we require attestation evidence for any host that unseals customer KEKs. Do you support TPM/HSM attestation on your on‑prem package or will we need a vendor‑supplied appliance?

2) Telemetry redaction: please include the paragraph Kimberly requested. We expect a clear list of fields that are never included in logs or are always masked.

3) Break‑glass escalation: provide the exact notification chain and SLA for post‑event reviews. We need to ensure audits can be completed within 30 days of an event.

If you can update the playbook and send the revised artifacts and a short summary (1 page) of the changes, we can get legal review started next week.

Best,
Sarah

Sarah Lin

Northfield Health
